evidence.title: Cline Cloud Agents
evidence.locator: Getting started; Run several agents at once; Check in from your phone; Choose a model; How your work is saved; Steering the agent; Security; Limits; Current limitations
evidence.finding: Browser client at app.cline.bot needs a Cline account and GitHub connection; pick repo, branch and model in the Agents tab. Each session gets its own isolated sandbox and cline/ branch, commits and pushes as it goes and opens a PR on request. Sidebar shows working, done and waiting sessions. Works in mobile browsers to read progress, answer questions and send follow-ups. Model can be switched mid-session; providers ClineFree, ClinePass, Cline credits. Idle 15 minutes pauses the sandbox, reopening resumes with workspace intact; work continues after the tab closes. GitHub access limited to the chosen repo. Up to 10 running sessions and 50 new sessions per day; at capacity users are asked to retry. Rules, skills, MCP servers and connectors are not loaded in cloud sessions.

evidence.title: Kanban Core Workflow
evidence.locator: 1. Create Tasks through 6. Clean Up; Workflow Summary
evidence.finding: Cards are created manually or by the sidebar agent, which can create and link cards and start them. Cmd/Ctrl-click links cards; when a linked card completes and is trashed the next linked task starts automatically. Play creates an ephemeral git worktree, symlinks gitignored files such as node_modules (edits to them hit the main copy), runs the agent in its own terminal, and the card shows the latest message or tool call. Detail view shows the agent TUI and a diff with checkpoint-scoped message ranges; inline diff comments go back to the agent. Commit or Open PR prompts the agent, which handles merge conflicts. Trash removes the worktree and keeps a resume ID.

evidence.title: Kanban overview
evidence.locator: Warning; Prerequisites; Key Capabilities; Agent Compatibility
evidence.finding: Kanban is a research preview started with npx kanban from a git repo root; it opens a local board. Works with Cline CLI, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and related runtimes available in settings.

evidence.title: Auto Approve & YOLO Mode
evidence.locator: How It Works; Permissions; Safe vs Approval-Required Commands; Recommendations; YOLO Mode
evidence.finding: Auto-approve is evaluated per tool call by category (read/edit project files, read/edit all files outside workspace, safe/all commands, browser, MCP). The model sets a requires_approval flag per command; there is no fixed allowlist. Optional OS notifications fire when approval is required and when an auto-approved command has run for 30 seconds. Recommended default enables only Read project files. YOLO auto-approves everything, including file operations anywhere and mode transitions.

evidence.title: Scheduling
evidence.locator: Warning; Schedule Wizard; Creating Schedules with Flags; Managing Schedules; Routing Results
evidence.finding: Applies to SDK, CLI and Kanban, not the VS Code/JetBrains extensions. Cron schedules run through the local hub, persist across process restarts and run independently of a terminal session. Options include --timeout, --max-parallel (default 1; runs that come due while busy wait their turn) and --mode (default yolo; scheduled runs approve their own tool calls). Commands list, trigger, pause, resume, update, history (status, duration, tokens, cost), stats (success rate, last failure), delete, export/import. A running connector can post results to a chat.

evidence.title: Checkpoints
evidence.locator: How It Works; Viewing and Comparing Changes; Restoring Checkpoints; Checkpoints and Message Editing
evidence.finding: A shadow Git repository records a checkpoint after each tool use, separate from project history; checkpoints persist across editor sessions. Compare opens a diff per checkpoint. Restore Files, Restore Task Only (deletes later messages) or both. Editing a previous message and choosing Restore All reverts files before resubmitting.

evidence.title: Tasks
evidence.locator: What are Tasks; Understanding Task Costs; Task History; Resuming Tasks
evidence.finding: Each task has a unique ID and storage directory, full conversation history, token usage, estimated API cost in the task header and execution time. History is saved locally, searchable and sortable by cost or tokens; tasks resume with full context across sessions.

evidence.title: Auto Compact
evidence.locator: How It Works; Cost Considerations; Restoring Context
evidence.finding: Near the context limit Cline summarizes the conversation and replaces history with the summary; the summarization call shows its cost. Other models fall back to rule-based truncation. Checkpoints can restore pre-summary state.

evidence.title: Subagents
evidence.finding: CLI and Desktop only. spawn_agent starts a child with its own context and mode tools; in Plan mode shell commands that usually change files are refused but others such as python -c can still write. evidence.title: Connectors

evidence.finding: CLI only. Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, WhatsApp and Linear connectors; each incoming message (via platform webhooks or sockets) creates or continues an agent session and replies in the thread. Discord /abort stops the current task and normal messages steer an active task. Access can be restricted by user ID or a hook command. Connectors need the local hub.

evidence.title: CLI Reference

evidence.finding: Prompts run in yolo mode by default (--auto-approve true); --id resumes a session; -t timeout; -z runs in the background hub; --worktree creates a detached worktree; --acp mode.
